function: Predicts top-M mmWave beam indices from a 64-beam codebook using GPS position, camera images and LiDAR point clouds, to shrink the beam sweep (p. 5-6, 9).
system: V2I and V2V at 60 GHz; receiver has a 16-element ULA phased array with 64 codebook beams, transmitter one antenna; OFDM; no RIS (p. 5, 9).
method: Multi-modal network: 1D CNN for position, fine-tuned EfficientNet-B0 for images, fine-tuned PointNet for LiDAR; concatenation, two dense layers, softmax; supervised cross-entropy, Adam (p. 6-9).
data_channel: DeepSense 6G measured data, scenarios 31-34 (V2I) and 36-39 (V2V), 60 GHz, Arizona day and night; no simulated channel (p. 9).
test_conditions: Each scenario split 60/20/20 for training, validation, test, a separate model per scenario; results averaged over 5 runs; no cross-scenario test (p. 9-10).
baselines: 5G-NR exhaustive beam sweep (non-learned), compared on sweeping latency and search space only; no learned baseline compared (p. 11-12).
metrics: Top-M accuracy (M=1, 5, 9, 13), received power ratio, beam sweeping latency and search-space overhead, inference time per sample (p. 10-13).
complexity: Measured inference time of roughly 0.5 to 1.0 ms per sample on an RTX 2080 GPU; no FLOPs or parameter count (p. 13).
openness: Code and data preprocessing at https://github.com/mbaqer/V2X-mmWave-Beamforming; DeepSense 6G public dataset (p. 9-10).
q1_support: p. 9: "dataset [64], [65], a collection of real-world mmWave"
q2_support: p. 9: "split the data resources of each scenario into 60%, 20%,"; p. 10: "we then train the model on splitted training samples of each" - train and test come from the same scenario; no unseen scenario, band or site is tested.
q3_support: p. 12: "approach against standard defined existing beam selection" - only the 5G-NR exhaustive search is compared, on sweeping latency and search space; no earlier learned method is compared, and Table II (p. 4) lists related works without results.
q5_support: p. 10: "The data preprocessing and implementation codes along with"; p. 10: "https://github.com/mbaqer/V2X-mmWave-Beamforming"
notes: Included, area 3: the learned output is the beam index for a codebook (p. 5-6). Area 5 (ISAC) was considered and not applied because the beams serve communication only, with GPS, camera and LiDAR used as non-RF side information (p. 5); the reviewer should confirm. q1: real-world DeepSense 6G measurements (p. 9). q2 is 0: the paper itself says adaptability to suburban or rural scenarios still has to be addressed (p. 11). q3 is 0: the only comparison is with the non-learned 5G-NR exhaustive search, on latency and search space (Fig. 7, p. 12), and there is no learned baseline. q4 rests on the measured inference time (p. 13); the beam sweeping time of Eqs. 14-15 is signaling overhead and is not counted. q5: the paper states that code and preprocessing are public on GitHub (p. 10) and uses the public DeepSense 6G dataset (p. 9). Top-13 accuracy is up to 98.19% for V2I but only 66.96% for V2V (p. 11).
